segments.speaker: Ana Duarte
segments.text: Quick sync. Two things: the beta feedback, and whether we hold or move the launch date.

segments.speaker: Jonas Weber
segments.text: Beta feedback is better than I expected. Nineteen of twenty-four testers used it more than once, which is the number I actually care about.

segments.speaker: Ana Duarte
segments.text: What did the five who didn't come back say?

segments.speaker: Jonas Weber
segments.text: Four of them never finished setup. One said it did what they wanted on the first try and they had no reason to return, which is arguably a compliment.

segments.speaker: Sofia Marchetti
segments.text: Setup is the thing then. If four of five churned before finishing setup, the product is fine and the front door is broken.

segments.speaker: Ana Duarte
segments.text: Jonas, can you pull the setup funnel by step so we can see exactly where they stop?

segments.speaker: Jonas Weber
segments.text: I'll pull the step-by-step setup funnel and share it before Thursday.

segments.speaker: Ana Duarte
segments.text: Second thing. The launch date. We said the fourteenth. Do we still believe it?

segments.speaker: Sofia Marchetti
segments.text: Sales does. We have three customers who've been told the fourteenth. Moving it costs more credibility than shipping something imperfect.

segments.speaker: Jonas Weber
segments.text: Engineering can hit the fourteenth if setup is the only thing we change. If we add anything else, it slips.

segments.speaker: Ana Duarte
segments.text: Then we agreed: the date holds, and setup is the only change that goes in. Everything else waits.

segments.speaker: Sofia Marchetti
segments.text: I'll tell the three customers the date is confirmed so nobody is guessing.
